# Evaluating ∫ -2*sin(x)*cos(x) dx

## Method: Substitution

I'll use the substitution $u = \sin(x)$, so $du = \cos(x)\, dx$.

$$\int -2\sin(x)\cos(x)\, dx = \int -2u \, du$$

$$= -2 \cdot \frac{u^2}{2} + C = -u^2 + C$$

Substituting back:

$$= -\sin^2(x) + C$$

## Verification by Differentiation

$$\frac{d}{dx}\left[-\sin^2(x) + C\right] = -2\sin(x)\cos(x) \checkmark$$

<answer>-sin(x)**2 + C</answer>
